Following are lipid lab results collected between 2009 and 2020, including some overseas.  (Kaiser has US labs, except Litholink, since 2014)

Appreciate if you review the labs.  I think I see a pattern that follows level of indoor rowing and dairy consumption, esp in very recent years.

Before making any changes to medicine, I would like to see what I can do myself (diet + exercise).  
I prefer less, not more medicine, but accept medicine if the benefit exceeds what I can (reliably) do myself.


Appreciate if you answer:
(1) When (date) to repeat lipid test (fasting, much less cheese, and no Gemfibrozil)

(2)  If latest numbers (Total = 165, Tri=83, HDL = 58, LDL = 90) could be better, tell me what you would like?  (Be as specific as you can) 

(3) Do you see any numbers in the history, that you DO LIKE?  (Assume for moment I can reproduce them)

(4) Aside from "numbers", is there something statin provides BEYOND these numbers, ie put it into the water supply (heard this many years back)

After importing the data, I clean and organize the data.
```{r, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)
library(readr)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(kableExtra)
library(gt)

# setup
# -------------------------------------
the_dir <- "~/code/health_labs/DATA/"
the_file <- "2021_03_19_ongoing_Health_Time_Series_RAW_LABS_from_Google.csv"
the_path  <- glue::glue(the_dir, the_file)
# -------------------------------------
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
# convert missing to NA; do not report col_types
import_data  <- function(the_path=NULL){
    readr::read_csv(the_path, na = c("", NA), show_col_types=FALSE)
}
the_data  <- tibble::as_tibble(import_data(the_path))

##  As stored, Date is character in form d m y
the_data <- the_data |> mutate(Date = lubridate::dmy(Date))

#   Convert character to numeric (warnings will replace with NA)
the_data <- the_data |> dplyr::mutate(Test_Result = as.numeric(Test_Result))

#  if Test_Result = NA, change to 0
the_data <- the_data |> dplyr::mutate(Test_Result = ifelse(is.na(Test_Result),0,Test_Result))

#   Check for Duplicates
the_data %>% count(Date, Test_Name, sort=T) |> head()
#         Date Test_Name n
# 1 2018-08-13  Serum_Cr 3
# 2 2019-05-28  Serum_Cr 2
# 3 2020-05-07  Serum_Ca 2
# 4 2009-04-02       BUN 1
# 5 2009-04-02       GLU 1
# 6 2009-04-02       HDL 1

# 2020-01-17 has 2 rows; 1 for Tot_Cholesterol; 1 for HDL, LDL
the_data |> dplyr::filter(Date == as.Date("2020-01-17"))

##  By data, check duplicates (was 404 x 10)
the_data |> dplyr::filter(Date == dmy("13Aug2018") & Test_Name=="Serum_Cr")

# rows to remove; now 402 x 10
z1 <- the_data |> dplyr::filter_out(Date == dmy("13Aug2018") & 
  Test_Name=="Serum_Cr" & (Comment != "Litholink")) 
the_data <- z1
# ------------------------------------ Data now "clean"

```

```{r, include=FALSE}
# Extract lipid results from data.  For cholesterol, limit to need to "VLDL", "LDL", "HDL", "Trig"
# Drop non-lipid columns

values <- c("VLDL", "LDL", "HDL", "Tot_Cholesterol", "Trig")
cholesterol_data <- 
  the_data |> dplyr::filter(Test_Name %in% values) |>
  dplyr::select(c(-Code,-Normal, -Allopurinol, -Where, -Purpose, -Comment, -`Exercise Level`)) |> 
  arrange(Date, Test_Name)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Add data since 2020 
# Date, HDL, LDL, Tot_Cholesterol, Trig, VLDL
add_data <- data.frame(Date =  (as.Date(c("2020-02-20", "2022-09-01", "2026-01-17"))),
                       Tot_Cholesterol = c(151,131,165),
                       HDL = c(51,52,58),
                       LDL = c(78,64,90),
                       VLDL = c(NA,NA,NA),
                       Trig = c(111,73,83)
)

# wide to longer
add_data <- add_data |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!Date, names_to = "Test_Name", values_to = "Test_Result")

cholesterol_data <- rbind(cholesterol_data,add_data )
```



Display lipids data:
```{r }
#| echo: false

# use wide
cholesterol_wide <- 
  cholesterol_data |> tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Test_Name, values_from = Test_Result)

gt_tbl <- gt(cholesterol_wide)
res <-
  gt_tbl |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Cholesterol",
    subtitle = "patient: jim"
  ) |>
  cols_move(
    columns = Tot_Cholesterol,
    after = Date
  ) |> 
  fmt_date(
    columns = Date,
    date_style = "iso"
  )
 tab_source_note(
    source_note = "Numbers are not the whole story.  I have control over diet/exercise.  Most of my adult life fat and certainly satuarated fats were to be avoided.  More recently oxalate was dominant threat, but Low-oxalate diet is extremely difficult, especially on mostly vegetarian diet.   As fats became less ostracied, I drifted into a high fat (dairy) diet for protein and to satiate, a role pre-oxalate played by nuts, seeds, soy and many beans.  HDL rose! ."
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = md("Miraculously, my November '25 urine oxalate showed in normal range!  In past week, I cut way  back on amount of daily, especially cheese, and put more beans in place.")
  )
res
```
